title: Establishment of Axenic Sea-Ice Diatom Cultures
author: Anders Torstensson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qvzdw76

steps.title: Vortex and sonicate culture
steps.instruction: Place an optically dense diatom culture on ice, vortex‑mix for 3 min at < 8 °C, then ultrasonicate on ice for 30 s at 80 % amplitude in 5‑second pulses to detach attached bacteria and EPS aggregates.

substeps.instruction: Ultrasonicate 30 s, 80 % amplitude, 5‑s pulses, on ice

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash twice
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the treated cells at 1000 × g for 10 min at < 8 °C, discard supernatant, and wash the pellet twice with sterile F/2 medium (Guillard, 1975) to remove the majority of loose bacterial cells.

substeps.instruction: First wash with sterile F/2 medium
Second wash with sterile F/2 medium

steps.title: Add antibiotics and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the six antibiotics listed in Table 1 to the F/2 medium, resuspend the cells, and incubate for 5 days at –1 °C under light of 20–45 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and wash
steps.instruction: After the antibiotic incubation, centrifuge the culture again at 1000 × g for 10 min at < 8 °C and wash the pellet once with fresh sterile F/2 medium.

steps.title: Isolate <10 cells
steps.instruction: Using a pipette or by plating on F/2 agar, pick fewer than ten cells to start axenic cultures (single‑cell colonies).

steps.title: Grow and test for bacteria
steps.instruction: Allow the cultures to recover and grow for approximately two months, then assess bacterial contamination by DAPI staining and by plating on half‑strength BD Difco™ Marine Agar 2216 kept at < 8 °C; the agar should be prepared with artificial seawater containing 411 mM NaCl, 9.39 mM KCl, 26.1 mM MgCl₂·6H₂O, 28.4 mM MgSO₄·7H₂O, and 5.01 mM TAPSO buffer.

substeps.instruction: Plate on half‑strength BD Difco™ Marine Agar 2216

steps.title: Repeat if contamination persists
steps.instruction: If bacterial cells are still detected, repeat the entire protocol; axenic cultures are usually established within the first or second attempt.
